questions.scenario: You plan to eat one cup of soup. Tomato soup has 300 mg of sodium in each half cup. Vegetable soup has 450 mg of sodium in each full cup. Which soup has less sodium in one cup?

options.text: Tomato soup
Vegetable soup
They have the same amount

questions.explanation: Check the serving size on the label. One cup of tomato soup is two half cups, so it has 600 mg of sodium. One cup of vegetable soup has 450 mg, which is less.

questions.scenario: Two kinds of crackers have the same serving size. The label on cracker A says 4% Daily Value for sodium. The label on cracker B says 22%. What does this tell you?

options.text: Cracker A is low in sodium. Cracker B is high in sodium.
Both crackers are low in sodium.
The % Daily Value cannot be used to compare foods.

questions.explanation: On a food label, 5% Daily Value or less in one serving is low, and 20% or more is high. This compares only sodium, not everything about the crackers.

questions.scenario: A yogurt label says Total Sugars 12 g. The next line says Includes 5 g Added Sugars. How much sugar is in one serving in total?

options.text: 5 g

questions.explanation: Added sugars are already counted in total sugars, so do not add them again. One serving has 12 g of sugar in total, and 5 g of that is added sugar.

questions.scenario: A cereal label lists one serving as three-quarters of a cup. Does that tell you how much cereal you should eat?

options.text: No. It shows about how much people usually eat, not how much you should eat.
Yes. It is the right amount for everyone.
Yes. It is the most anyone should eat at one time.

questions.explanation: The serving size is the amount people usually eat at one time. It is not advice on how much you should eat. If you eat more or less, the nutrient amounts change too.

questions.scenario: A generally healthy adult aged 65 or older walks briskly for 150 minutes each week. What else does CDC activity advice include for this age?

options.text: Nothing else. Walking is enough.
Only more walking, every day
Muscle strengthening 2 days a week, plus balance activities

questions.explanation: For adults 65 and older, CDC advice adds muscle-strengthening activities on at least 2 days a week, plus balance activities such as walking heel-to-toe or standing up from a sitting position. Choose activities that fit what you can do safely.

questions.scenario: You are making a salad and cooking raw chicken in the same kitchen. Which is the safer way to do it?

options.text: Use a separate cutting board for the raw chicken
Wash the raw chicken in the sink first
Cut the salad on the same board right after the chicken

questions.explanation: Do not wash raw chicken. Washing can splash germs onto your sink and salad. Use a separate cutting board for raw chicken, and cook chicken to 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). Check with a food thermometer.

options.text: Taste them to decide
Heat them well and eat them
Throw them away

questions.explanation: CDC advises eating refrigerated restaurant leftovers within 3 to 4 days and throwing them away after that. Five days is past that time.
